name: Product manager
description: Prioritization, discovery, and influence: for people who decide what gets built and why.
guidance: Probe for decisions, evidence, and trade-offs rather than process vocabulary. Ask about something they chose not to build and how they defended it. Ask how they learned what users needed: who they talked to, what surprised them, and what they changed as a result. Push on metrics: which number they were trying to move, why that one, and what happened to it. Ask about a launch that underperformed and what they did in the following two weeks. Explore influence without authority through a specific disagreement with engineering or leadership. Ask how AI tools have changed how they research, write, or prototype, and what they still do by hand. Weak answers describe frameworks; strong answers describe a specific bet, who disagreed, and what the data later showed.
examples: Tell me about something you decided not to build that people wanted. How did you make the case, and were you right?
Walk me through the last time talking to users changed your roadmap. What did you hear, and what did you drop?
Describe a launch that missed its goal. What did you do in the two weeks after?
An engineer tells you your top priority will take three times longer than planned. Walk me through the conversation.
Which metric did your last project aim to move, why that one, and what would have made you abandon it?
